entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision
entries.title: Caluza v. Brown - Benefit of the Doubt Standard
entries.content:
Established that when evidence is in approximate balance, the benefit of the doubt must be given to the claimant. This is a fundamental principle in VA disability claims.

Legal Principle: Benefit of the doubt applies when evidence is in approximate balance

Categories: Evidence, Benefit of the Doubt

Year: 1995

metadata.principle: Benefit of the doubt applies when evidence is in approximate balance

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision
entries.title: Fenderson v. West - Duty to Assist
entries.content:
Clarified VA's duty to assist claimants in developing evidence for their claims, including obtaining relevant medical records and providing medical examinations.

Legal Principle: VA has duty to assist in developing claims

Categories: Duty to Assist, Evidence Development

Year: 1999

metadata.principle: VA has duty to assist in developing claims

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision
entries.title: Gilbert v. Derwinski - Service Connection Requirements
entries.content:
Established the three-part test for service connection: (1) current disability, (2) in-service incurrence or aggravation, and (3) nexus between the two.

Legal Principle: Three elements required for service connection

Categories: Service Connection, Evidence

Year: 1990

metadata.principle: Three elements required for service connection

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision
entries.title: Hickson v. West - Lay Testimony Competence

Year: 1999

metadata.principle: Lay testimony can be competent for observable symptoms

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision

Year: 2007

metadata.principle: Continuity of symptomatology can establish service connection

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision
entries.title: Nieves-Rodriguez v. Peake - Medical Treatise Evidence

Categories: Evidence, Medical Opinion

Year: 2008

metadata.principle: Medical treatises can be substantial evidence

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision

Year: 1991

metadata.principle: VA must provide adequate reasons for denial

entries.source: Board of Veterans' Appeals - Precedential Decision

Year: 1995

metadata.principle: VA must notify claimants of evidence needed

Year: 2014

metadata.principle: Medical opinions must be based on accurate facts

metadata.principle: Effective date rules for rating increases

metadata.principle: Timing requirements for VCAA notice

metadata.principle: Presumption of medical examiner competence
